description: Behavioural obligations for v0.5 delivery honesty — the §14.2 terminal states, bounce coverage on session death, the §7 undeliverable auto-resolutions, and receipt semantics. The anti-false-belief invariant: at no point can 'it's fine' and 'nobody will ever see this' present identically to a sender.
obligation: BOUNCE COVERAGE (§14.2/§16.3): (1) When a session goes terminal (closed or expired, incl. the §16.4 human kill-switch), EVERY un-acked session-addressed COMMAND entry — directives and `message` entries alike — MUST transition to `bounced`, not only undelivered ones: entries a bridge drained but never acked (the §13.4 crash window) bounce too, because a terminal session can never re-drain and 'delivered-but-unacked to a dead session' would otherwise read as delivered forever. (2) The receipt's `prior` preserves the distinction: `queued` = never seen; `delivered` = seen-then-orphaned — and the sender's surfaced delivery record states it EXPLICITLY: any surfaced §14.2 delivery record (the §8.2 GET's `mailbox` track — schematized as `mailbox.prior` — or a Hub's directive-delivery view) SHOULD carry the explicit `prior` field on its `bounced` terminal, stamped ONCE at the bounce transition and MUST equal the bounce receipt's `prior` (one stamp, two surfaces, no re-derivation drift); `prior: "delivered"` SHOULD co-occur with `delivered_at`, and the legacy delivered_at-presence inference survives only as the consumer's fallback when `prior` is absent (a replica predating the marker sends nothing). (3) Principal-addressed entries do NOT bounce on a single session's death (a sibling rescues them via visibility-timeout redelivery) — but the orphan still terminates: a principal-addressed entry whose retention lapses while delivered-but-unacked transitions to `bounced` with prior `delivered` and the receipt's `session` naming the last claimant; one never drained at retention end takes the ordinary `expired` terminal. (4) `response` and `receipt` entries NEVER bounce — they are delivery conveniences over durably-held state: an un-acked response entry on a dead session is superseded by the unchanged §8.2 pull path (no bounce, no receipt); an undeliverable receipt is nothing at all. AUTO-RESOLUTION (§7): (5) On EITHER undeliverable delivery-track terminal — `bounced` OR `expired` (mailbox retention lapsed while queued) — an addressed ask auto-resolves `cancelled` and a task `dismissed`, with Hub-attested `response.actor: "system:undeliverable"`, riding the same atomic first-terminal-wins CAS (a harmless no-op returning the existing Response when the addressee already resolved, or when message-level expires_at already fired §7 expiry). Delivery-track expiry emits NO receipt in v0.5 (`receipt.event` carries only `bounced`; the §8.2 pull is authoritative for expiry). RECEIPTS (§8.7.1): (6) Receipts are best-effort, delivered only to LIVE sessions of the sender, deduplicated by the recipient on (in_reply_to, event), and MUST NOT themselves generate receipts — no cascade; the sender's §8.2 pull remains authoritative. A bounced ask's auto-cancellation `response` entry and its bounce `receipt` may sit in the same sender mailbox for the same in_reply_to with non-colliding ack keys (res_ vs rcpt_). TRACK TRUTHFULNESS (§14.2): (7) `expired` on a delivery track MUST mean never delivered — on the mailbox track (never drained) AND the ask/task response track (retention passed short of delivered-to-agent: the human's answer was never seen). (8) Once `delivered`, later expiry of the RESOLUTION track never rewrites the delivery track: resolution-expired + delivery-delivered = seen-but-unanswered; delivery-expired = never seen. (9) `delivered`/`delivered-to-agent` requires the receiving party actually getting it: first drain (never a bare stream push, dp-021) for mailbox entries; push 2xx or the agent's authenticated GET for a Response. (10) The delivery track never gates or alters the §7 resolution — the bounce auto-resolution is a §7 transition TRIGGERED by the track, not a rewrite of it.
